A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices. Despite the changed title and AnythingNER-to-DynamicNER renaming, the shared CascadeNER framework, category hierarchy and benchmark experiments establish that these are revisions of the same work.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual NER results in Tables 1–3, ablations in Appendix C and additional CascadeNER results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v4 reports original NER comparisons, categorization-quality experiments, ablations and calculated API-cost results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: CascadeNER's extraction, union fusion and contextual hierarchical classification are retained. However, dynamic categorization changes from annotation-guided adjustments and subsequent statistical balancing in v1 Appendix A to an automated four-round procedure with stage-specific metric guidance in v4 Section 3 and Appendices A–B. This substantially changes the proposed dataset-construction method.

E1.justification: The eight languages, 8/31/155 category hierarchy and five external benchmarks are retained. Beyond v1's standard BIO/GEIC in-house comparison, v4 explicitly evaluates recognition with dynamically varying category lists, extending the test scenario. Dynamic categorization itself already existed in v1's training data.

E2.justification: GEMNET and LS-unLLaMA disappear from the in-house comparison, while v4 provides quantitative PromptNER comparisons where v1 reported hallucinations preventing results. LS-unLLaMA is also removed from the corresponding external-benchmark comparisons: v1 Tables 2–3 versus v4 Tables 6–7. These changes substantially revise comparator membership.

E3.justification: The dataset split changes from approximately 3:1:1 to 1:1:3; English changes from 900/300/300 to 300/300/900 train/dev/test sentences. External CascadeNER settings change from Qwen2-1.5B with 50 demonstrations to Qwen2.5-7B with 3, and GPT baselines are specified as GPT-4o. v4 also introduces controlled base/dynamic learning comparisons and categorization-quality metrics. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds comparisons of base, random and optimized categorization across languages, plus a comparative API-cost analysis. Conversely, v1's demonstration-count sensitivity study and mixed-size extractor/classifier configurations disappear. Result-fusion and contextual-classification ablations remain, while the base-model analysis is revised.

E5.justification: v4 Section 5.1 newly reports averaging five independent tests for random categorization. v1 provides no corresponding independent-run reporting. Neither version supplies model-result confidence intervals or comparable run-to-run uncertainty estimates; extraction repetitions are algorithmic operations, not independent experimental runs.

E6.justification: v4 replaces and expands the in-house result matrices under different settings in Tables 3–4, and adds categorization-quality outcomes and calculated costs: GPT-NER $513.92, PromptNER $128.49 and CascadeNER $45.86 in Table 11. v1's separate 100-shot best-result tables are removed. The retained external-benchmark tables otherwise preserve their numerical scores despite changed stated settings, so these do not establish comparable-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix A adds mathematical definitions for cohesion, normalized entropy, Gini coefficient and coefficient of variation. The existing fusion, hierarchical-classification and sampling equations remain, and no theorem or proof is added. The printed cohesion normalization is inconsistent with its stated range and 0.9 merging threshold.

C1.justification: v1 presents GEIC as a newly introduced task and foregrounds CascadeNER. v4 drops GEIC as a separate contribution and centers DynamicNER, automated quality-preserving categorization and effective evaluation of LLM generalization. CascadeNER is repositioned as a lightweight method addressing shortcomings revealed by the benchmark.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of category knowledge leaking through few-shot demonstrations, conflicts between categorization metrics, and model-dependent strengths and weaknesses of reasoning-based methods. It also discusses overlap between Wikipedia-derived datasets and its mitigation. The flat-NER and eight-language limitations, and supervised methods' advantages in some settings, largely persist.

D1.justification: v4 adds Wikipedia-API collection and midpoint balancing details, BERT-based metric computation and thresholds, GPT-4o-generated and manually checked PromptNER training material, and Sentence-BERT filtering above similarity 0.8 with replacement annotation. Conversely, v1's SWIFT fine-tuning framework and explicit GPT-4o annotation-review disclosure disappear. The shared repository link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 substantially revises research positioning around dataset design, generalization, reasoning and privacy, replacing much of v1's small-language-model background. It newly acknowledges prior two-stage NER methods by Shen et al. (2021) and Wu et al. (2022), and adds literature supporting categorization and CoT discussions. This changes the novelty context, beyond bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around DynamicNER. Dataset construction moves ahead of CascadeNER, the standalone GEIC section disappears, external-benchmark material moves into Appendix D, and limitations receive a separate section. Terminology and the author list also change.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the main experimental display with new result matrices and multilingual categorization-quality panels, adds a categorization pipeline and cost table, and relocates retained benchmark tables. The GEIC-versus-sequence-labeling diagram, GEIC-format example, demonstration-count plot and best-result tables disappear. The fusion plot is redrawn, and the model-ablation table is restructured.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful controlled comparisons, cost evidence, prior-work attribution and overlap-filtering documentation. However, legacy scores remain unchanged despite revised model and demonstration settings, leaving their experimental provenance unexplained. Its new cohesion formula in Appendix A, Equation 3, has maximum 0.5 despite a stated merging threshold of 0.9, weakening confidence in the central categorization procedure. Together with removed sensitivity evidence, these unresolved reporting and mathematical issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the PDFs.
